# Actual critical shared caps admit a physical second-order descent

This extends the planar path in candidate 3ff8967854167565 to genuine critical cap budgets and to every continuous dimension \(d\ge2\). It gives a local exclusion for one explicit family. It does not classify fixed-cap maximizers or prove OC.

## 1. An actual three-fiber family with a known exact critical cover

Let
\[
T=\operatorname{conv}\{0,e_1,\ldots,e_d\},\quad
V=1/d!,\quad g=\frac1{d+1}{\bf1},\quad K=T-g,
\quad \Gamma=(d/(d+1))^d.
\]
Fix \(0<r<1\). At integer bases \(-1,0,1\), use
\[
rK,\quad K,\quad rK.
\tag{1}
\]
These are the exact integer fibers of their convex hull. The midpoint inclusion is strict because \(rK\subset\operatorname{int}K\). Total mixed mass is \(M_0=V(1+2r^d)\).

Define the fixed linear margins on centered continuous coordinates
\[
\ell_0(x)=-\sum_{j=1}^d x_j,\qquad
\ell_i(x)=x_i\quad(1\le i\le d),
\]
and the cylindrical caps \(H_i=\{\ell_i(x)\ge0\}\). Since their margins sum to zero, these \(d+1\) caps cover the entire ambient space, not just the original body. Each has mass
\[
D=\Gamma V(1+2r^d)=\Gamma M_0.
\tag{2}
\]

This is the actual maximum-depth value, not an artificially enlarged budget. At the actual middle centroid \((0,0)\), its own fiber pays \(\Gamma V\). The equal-copy paired-centroid-tail theorem pays \(2\Gamma r^dV\) from the two endpoints for every nonvertical through-point cap. A vertical cap pays at least \(V(1+r^d)\ge D\). Thus every containing cap has mass at least \(D\). Conversely the fixed caps \(H_i\), each of mass \(D\), cover every actual candidate and bound its depth above by \(D\). The initial normalized maximum is exactly \(\Gamma\).

The same positive first-order cap multipliers
\[
\lambda_i=\frac1{(d+1)\Gamma}
\]
give the support-facet stress on all three homothetic simplices. On any facet, each of the \(d\) other caps covers the fraction \((d/(d+1))^{d-1}\); their multiplier-weighted sum is exactly one. No critical cap coincides with a body facet, and midpoint compatibility has strict slack.

## 2. Physical endpoint simplices and exact cap formulas

Put
\[
a_d=\frac{d-1}{3},\qquad
b_d=\frac{(d-1)(2d+3)}{6(d+1)},\qquad
q=a_dt^2,\quad L=1+b_dt^2,\quad s_\pm=q\pm t.
\]
Replace only the two endpoints by
\[
r(T_\pm(t)-g),\qquad
T_\pm(t)=\operatorname{conv}\{s_\pm{\bf1},Le_1,\ldots,Le_d\},
\tag{3}
\]
while keeping the middle fiber \(K\) fixed.

For sufficiently small \(|t|\), these are positively oriented full-dimensional simplices; \(s_\pm<1/(d+1)<L\) and \(L-ds_\pm>0\). Since the original endpoint \(rK\) is compactly contained in \(\operatorname{int}K\), continuity of the finitely many vertices makes both deformed endpoints remain inside \(\operatorname{int}K\). Their Minkowski average is then contained in \(K\), so the convex hull has exactly these three integer fibers. No forced intermediate mass is discarded.

Write \(h=d/(d+1)\) and \(g_0=1/(d+1)\). For a simplex \(T_s=\operatorname{conv}\{s{\bf1},Le_1,\ldots,Le_d\}\), the exact normalized volume is
\[
m(s,L)=|T_s|/V=L^{d-1}(L-ds).
\tag{4}
\]
In uncentered coordinates the fixed caps are \(\sum X_j\le h\) and \(X_i\ge g_0\). Each still strictly includes only its corresponding vertex. Edge-intersection ratios give their exact cap masses divided by \(V\):
\[
f_0(s,L)=\frac{L^{d-1}(h-ds)^d}{(L-ds)^{d-1}},
\qquad
f_i(s,L)=\frac{(L-ds)(L-g_0)^d}{L-s}\quad(i\ge1).
\tag{5}
\]
These formulas count every actual endpoint cap, including its unchanged translation by \(-g\) and its scale \(r^d\).

## 3. Exact second coefficients and a proved small interval

All expressions (4)–(5) are real analytic near \(t=0\). Pairing the two signs makes their sums even in \(t\). Direct expansion yields
\[
\frac{m(s_+,L)+m(s_-,L)}2
=1+\frac{d(d-1)}{6(d+1)}t^2+O(t^4),
\tag{6}
\]
\[
\frac{f_0(s_+,L)+f_0(s_-,L)}{2\Gamma}
=1-\frac{d(d-1)}6t^2+O(t^4),
\tag{7}
\]
\[
\frac{f_i(s_+,L)+f_i(s_-,L)}{2\Gamma}
=1-\frac{d-1}6t^2+O(t^4)\quad(i\ge1).
\tag{8}
\]

Here is explicit derivative algebra. Before substituting \(a_d,b_d\), the coefficient in (6) is \(d(b_d-a_d)\). For \(f_0/\Gamma\), the linear coefficient in the two branches is \(\mp2d\); exponentiating its logarithmic expansion gives quadratic coefficient \(d[(d-1)/2-2a_d]\). For \(f_i/\Gamma\), the linear coefficient is \(\mp(d-1)\), and its quadratic coefficient is \((d+1)b_d-(d-1)(a_d+1)\). These simplify exactly to (6)–(8).

All displayed second coefficients are nonzero for \(d\ge2\). Taylor's theorem therefore gives a positive interval \(0<|t|<\eta_d\) on which the pair's total volume is strictly greater than \(2V\) and every pair cap mass is strictly less than \(2\Gamma V\). For clarity, one can choose \(\eta_d\) small enough that the analytic remainder divided by \(t^2\) has absolute value less than half the smallest of the three positive coefficient magnitudes. Such an \(\eta_d>0\) exists by the displayed limits. Intersect this interval with the finite vertex-containment neighborhood from Section 2, obtaining \(\eta_{d,r}>0\).

Thus every \(0<|t|<\eta_{d,r}\) is a certified physical variation satisfying
\[
M(t)>M_0,\qquad \mu_t(H_i)<D\quad(0\le i\le d).
\tag{9}
\]
The caps and their budgets are fixed throughout. Since they still cover the entire space, the new normalized maximum depth is strictly less than \(D/M_0=\Gamma\). All first total cap and volume derivatives vanish; the simultaneous gain is second order.

More precisely, the coordinate caps dominate \(H_0\) for small nonzero \(t\), and the fixed cover gives
\[
\maxdepth(\mu_t)
\le \Gamma-
\frac{\Gamma r^d(d-1)(2d+1)}
{3(d+1)(1+2r^d)}t^2+O(t^4).
\tag{10}
\]
This is an upper expansion supplied by a genuine cover, not a claimed expansion of the actual optimized depth.

## 4. All caps in the standard critical/slack cover can be retained

If a separate whole-fiber circuit at every integer base is desired, adjoin the fixed endpoint caps
\[
H_{-i}=\{\ell_i(x)-(z+1)\ge0\},\qquad
H_{+i}=\{\ell_i(x)+(z-1)\ge0\}.
\tag{11}
\]
Each group covers the entire continuous space at its assigned endpoint. It strictly excludes both other original fibers: \(\max_K\ell_i=h<1\), and all endpoints are contained in \(K\). This remains true along the small path.

Give all these caps the same original critical upper budget \(D\), exactly as in the fixed-cap problem obtained from a critical/slack cover. Their initial masses are \(\Gamma r^dV<D\), so they remain strictly feasible for sufficiently small \(t\) by their explicit continuous cap formulas. The active caps (2) strictly decrease. Hence every original budget in this full cover is preserved.

This does not assert preservation of artificially tighter endpoint budgets equal to their smaller initial masses; such constraints would define a different variational problem. The original active/slack distinction is retained.

## 5. An explicit planar rational witness

For \(d=2\), the coefficients reduce exactly to \(q=t^2/3\), \(L=1+7t^2/18\), whose rational cap gaps were factored in the preceding physical-variation note. Set \(r=1/2\) and \(0<t\le1/10\). Both endpoint fibers lie strictly inside the middle \(K\): in uncentered middle coordinates their vertices are \((1-r)g+r v\). Their coordinates are positive, and their coordinate sums are less than one using \(L<101/100\), \(q+t<1/3\).

The original mass and critical budget are \(M_0=3/4\) and \(D=1/3\). At \(t=1/10\), the exact new values are
\[
M=\frac{1944713}{2592000},\qquad
\mu(H_0)=\frac{18538760053}{55663650000},
\]
\[
\mu(H_1)=\mu(H_2)=\frac{2772709845551}{8323432992000}.
\]
Every critical cap is below \(1/3\), and \(M>3/4\). The larger coordinate-cap ratio is
\[
\frac{2772709845551}{6244864330313}<\frac49,
\]
with exact difference \(25068711293/56203778972817\).

This body is explicitly OC-safe: the unchanged middle fiber has mass \(1/2>M/2\). Its own ordinary centroid therefore gives more than the target \(\Gamma_2M/2\) from that fiber alone.

## 6. Consequence and limitations

The family \(rK,K,rK\), \(0<r<1\), with a centered simplex \(K\), is not a local minimum of maximum normalized mixed depth in any \(d\ge2\), even when the comparison caps are fixed at an exact attained critical value. The construction couples masses from the two nonadjacent endpoint bases while retaining the full compatible middle fiber and every active critical budget.

There is one active critical circuit in this construction; the endpoint circuits are slack. No conclusion is supplied for interference between several deepest-site circuits or for active midpoint compatibility without strict slack. At \(r=1\), the endpoint perturbations generally force a larger, nontriangular middle fiber, so this proof cannot simply be continued through that boundary.

These limitations distinguish the proved physical second-order descent from an unproved classification of all extrema.
